name: Shihhi Arabic
notes:
Šiḥḥi Arabic of əlǦēdih, Ruʾūs al-Jibāl, Musandam (Oman). Primary reference Bernabela (2011), A Phonology and Morphology Sketch of the Šiḥḥi Arabic Dialect of əlǦēdih, Leiden MA thesis, read directly; each reflex below is quoted in its grapheme comment with the section and page.

WHY THIS IS NOT ar-OM. Two of the four reflexes cannot be expressed by the parent at all. ar-OM reads ⟨ع⟩ as [ʕ] alone, while Bernabela gives the glottal stop as the primary reflex of Old Arabic ʕ -- a loss that matters more for a grapheme table than anything in qāf, since it changes a consonant every text is full of. And ar-OM reads ⟨ظ⟩ as [ðˤ] alone, where Šiḥḥi has the plosive.

PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION, AND SAYING SO. Only the interdentals and ʕ are written here. The thesis sections stating the qāf, jīm and kāf reflexes were missing from the copy obtained, so those graphemes are left to the parent rather than guessed: ar-OM gives ⟨ق⟩ as [q, ɡ] and ⟨ج⟩ as [dʒ], and neither has been checked against Bernabela. What is known from the copy in hand is that /g/ is called a marginal phoneme occurring in loans from Gulf Arabic as a reflex of historical *q, which suggests ⟨ق⟩ is not [ɡ] natively -- suggestive, not sufficient, and deliberately not encoded. `quality` is `research` rather than `production` for that reason.

MSA INFLUENCE IS CARRIED, NOT RESOLVED. Bernabela notes interdental fricatives are occasionally heard and attributes them to MSA through the media and the mosque, so each interdental carries the plosive first and the fricative second rather than the spec choosing a register.
